aizanoi.name: Aizanoi
aizanoi.slogan: A Roman temple of Zeus still standing on the Anatolian plateau.
aizanoi.line: Its circular market hall carried a copy of Diocletian's Price Edict of AD 301, an attempt to stop runaway inflation.

afyonkalesi.name: Afyon Castle
afyonkalesi.slogan: A black volcanic crag that gave the city its name.
afyonkalesi.line: The rock rises 201 metres above town and was known to the Hittites as Hapanuwa.

afyonulucami.name: Afyon Ulu Cami
afyonulucami.slogan: Forty timber columns holding up a Seljuk prayer hall.
afyonulucami.line: Begun in 1272, its wooden hypostyle hall was named a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2023.

kutahyacinimuzesi.name: Kütahya Tile Museum
kutahyacinimuzesi.slogan: Cobalt, turquoise and a yellow all of its own.
kutahyacinimuzesi.line: Kütahya potters used a vibrant yellow never seen on Iznik ware, and took over from Iznik as Turkey's leading tile centre.

ayazini.name: Ayazini
ayazini.slogan: Churches and chambers carved straight into soft volcanic rock.
ayazini.line: Its name comes from the Greek Aya Sion, and a domed church is cut into the tuff at the village entrance.
